notes.title: In celebration of the anniversary of the game. ProtoCorgi Wiki is here!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/bbf86cedd058b8613e351752f0be49ac202db876.jpg[/img]
Mission Control here!

Today, June 15, marks the first anniversary of ProtoCorgi. In celebration, we are happy to announce the launch of the [url=https://protocorgi.wiki.gg/]ProtoCorgi Wiki[/url]!
Discover more about Bullet and his world in the detailed [url=https://protocorgi.wiki.gg/]ProtoCorgi Wiki[/url], now available at:
[url=https://protocorgi.wiki.gg/]https://protocorgi.wiki.gg/[/url]

While we are still working on some sections, everyone is invited to contribute to the wiki. Don't forget to follow the [url=https://protocorgi.wiki.gg/wiki/ProtoCorgi_Wiki:Rules]rules[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/7219a5345a2f1fa536ba7c40091d93498475bbaa.png[/img]

Overall the Wiki covers:
[list]
[*] [b]Stages:[/b] Descriptions of ProtoCorgi's campaign stages.
[*] [b]Enemies:[/b] Detailed information on [i]every[/i] enemy in ProtoCorgi.
[*] [b]Bosses:[/b]  Detailed information on [i]every[/i] boss in ProtoCorgi..
[*] [b]Mechanics:[/b] Information about [i]every[/i] ProtoCorgi system, from scoring systems to abilities.
[*] [b]Weapons:[/b] Detailed descriptions of [i]every[/i] weapons used by Bullet.
[*] [b]Lore:[/b] Background information on characters, world, and more.
[*] [b]Mutators:[/b] Version 1.1.0 exclusive feature, detailing every setting that alters the gameplay.
[*] [b]Unlockabes:[/b] Information about hidden features in ProtoCorgi that can be unlocked.
[*] [b]ProtoMaker:[/b] Information on game modding support.
[*] [b]Soundtrack:[/b] Details about the official ProtoCorgi Soundtrack.
[*] [b]Modding:[/b] About the game Modding support.
[*] [b]FAQ:[/b] The frequently asked questions has been moved here.
[*] [b]Changelogs:[/b] History of the different ProtoCorgi versions.
[*] [b]Credits:[/b] Information about all the people who worked to make ProtoCorgi a reality.
[/list]

And thanks to the wiki.gg team for making this possible!.

This concludes today’s transmission. However, remember that for the latest news about ProtoCorgi, follow us on our official [url=https://twitter.com/kemonogames]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://www.facebook.com/kemonogames/]Facebook[/url] pages, and if you want to meet the ProtoCorgi community, we’ve got you covered with our [url=http://discord.protocorgi.com/]Discord channel[/url] and our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1039280/discussions/]Steam forums[/url].

notes.title: Update 1.1. The Mutator Update has been released!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/6bc518138e6eda00fffb354bf3428b79d33b3386.png[/img]
Hello Everyone,

Mission Control here!
We are pleased to announce that [b]ProtoCorgi version 1.1[/b] is out!. This patch is composed of [b][i]new features[/i][/b] and improvements to the common issues we spotted in the game. Thanks to all of you for your feedback!. This patch has over a hundred fixes!. Here are the highlighted changes:

[h1][b]New Content:[/b][/h1]

[h2][b]Change gameplay rules with Mutators![/b][/h2]
Do you want to play against the time for score, a pacifist mode with his own rules, shoot only bark instead of using a turbo control, disable or revert features from the patch 1.1?, Mutators does that.

[h3][b]Caravan Mode Mutator:[/b][/h3]
[previewyoutube=lE7g6SVY4zI;full][/previewyoutube]
Bullet has a timebomb that will explode!. Adds time limit to the game. When active, add the timer to Campaign stage, Training Stages and ProtoCorgi Maker stages. This combined with the [i][b]Training power up selection[/b][/i] and abilities mutators, creates interesting short score runs. [i]Default value is OFF.[/i]

[h3][b]Unstoppable Caravan Mutator:[/b][/h3]
If activated, stop time doesn’t stop the caravan timer. [i]Default value is OFF.[/i]

[h3][b]Pacifist Mutator:[/b][/h3]
[previewyoutube=OSRJMC24-_w;full][/previewyoutube]
Disables damaging abilities from the player. [i]Default value is OFF.[/i]
Overhaul of the pacifist mode, now it's a real gamemode. Changes the following rules:
[list]
[*] Absorbed bullets give 10000 points.
[*] Absorbed bullets reduce the boss timer by 1 second for each one.
[*] Increased enemy bullets speed.
[*] Changes bosses patterns.
[*] Forces the game to one continue.
[/list]
If the game is completed in this mode, the pacifist achievement is always awarded.
As a recommendation, unlock all abilities before trying this mode, use absorb to reveal hidden chests and don't be ashamed to lower the difficulty.

[h3][b]Bark Only Mutator:[/b][/h3]
[previewyoutube=6EdIbvO0g8Y;full][/previewyoutube]
Players can only bark and use animal spirit/absorb/stop time/bombs. [i]Default value is OFF.[/i]
Changes the following rules:
[list]
[*] Hold shot replaced by a turbo bark. 
[*] Forces the game to one continue.
[/list]
This mutator is aimed to help users to unlock the Bark only achievement and collet 500 fruits achievement.

[h3][b]Hyper Bark Mutator:[/b][/h3]
[previewyoutube=2xLGvkRSXDc;full][/previewyoutube]
When the BARK bullet hits a chest or a fruit, the BARK powers up, increasing its damage and size. This can be chained. [i]Default value is ON.[/i]

[h3][b]Auto Bomb Mutator:[/b][/h3]
If the player has a bomb without use, that bomb is automatically used on death with a bit of invulnerability time instead of dying. Basically bombs are an extra life. [i]Default value is ON.[/i]

[h3][b]Score Extra Lives Mutator:[/b][/h3]
Get extra lives from the score!. Extra lives at 500000, 2000000, 5000000, 10000000, 25000000, 50000000, 75000000, 100000000 points and then for every 100000000 points. [i]Default value is ON.[/i]

[h3][b]Fruit Extra Lives Mutator:[/b][/h3]
Get extra lives for every 100 fruits!. [i]Default value is ON.[/i]

[i]Here is a video showcasing Auto Bomb, Score Extra lives, Fruit Extra lives and the new game over screen:[/i]
[previewyoutube=fBMaY8Xvpg0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3][b]Animal Spirit Mutator:[/b][/h3]
Enable or disable the animal spirit without resetting the game. [i]Default value is Enabled.[/i]

[h3][b] Absorb and Stop Time Mutator:[/b][/h3]
Enable Stop Time and absorb/Enable absorb/Disable. Changes the absorb/stop time state without resetting the game. [i]Default value is Enable Stop Time and absorb.[/i]

[h2][b]New Features![/b][/h2]
[h3][b]Sound Test Mode:[/b][/h3]
Bullet is hosting an intergalactic Party and you are invited!
At this party you can relax listening to the ProtoCorgi’s music and sounds!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/4604c63fb72e78976a756c07df3a0785e82299f2.png[/img]
 
[h3][b]Improved Game Soundtrack:[/b][/h3]
Inspired by the warm reception, [b]Francisco Cerda[/b] has achieved the seemingly impossible by enhancing ProtoCorgi’s soundtrack!. To hear a preview of the improvement, check out this video showcasing a comparison between the old and new version of the High Scores song:
[previewyoutube=nYrlpZw5sCA;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3][b]Power Up training selection:[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/f0f4747051df3954f52c62a8f3b1d41a29c05740.png[/img]
Select the starting power ups before a training stage!

[h3][b]Improved accesibility:[/b][/h3]
Revamped Pause menu! We know that some people have been confused by the original ProtoCorgi pause screen. To remedy that we decided to made a new redesigned pause menu. We changed the color of the message tooltip to brown and the possibility of modifying some options without the need to leave a session.
[previewyoutube=s0_7OWxESv0;full][/previewyoutube]
One of those new options is [b]brightness support[/b]. This change aims to make the game more accessible, as we heard some players had trouble distinguishing enemies, bullets and the background. We hope this can fix some visual problems on ProtoCorgi.
The new options are:
[b]Hitbox minimum opacity[/b] = how visible is the player hitbox when it is far from danger.
[b]Background brightness[/b] = self explained
[b]Effects brightness[/b] = brightness on explosions, particles, full screen explosions, etc
[b]Snack brightness[/b] = brightness of the snacks that orbit around Bullet’s combo
[b]Ally bullet brightness[/b] = brightness of player shots
[b]Score brightness[/b] = brightness of the score texts that come out when you get points

[h3][b]Code for State and Options of the game:[/b][/h3]
The game offers a code visible all the time that represents the state and options of the game, this was implemented for debugging purposes, but we exposed it for streamers and score runs.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/e7dbabb61fb416afe9132756aed3332e8e3de1a9.png[/img]
The code visible in the picture (C221000HASFAS-LP-) means a setting or achievement state for each letter.
Here is the list of possible values:
Letter 1: is Tutorial (L),is Training (T), is Training section (S), is Campaign (C), is a ProtoCorgi Maker Level (E)
Letter 2: Difficulty level, a number from 1 to 9, where 1 is easiest mode and 9 is the hardest.
Letter 3: Starting lives, a number from 1 to 9.
Letter 4: Starting continues, a number from 1 to 9.
Letter 5: Unstoppable caravan mutator enabled (U), Disabled (0)
Letter 6: Pacifist mutator enabled (P), Disabled (0)
Letter 7: Bark Only mutator enabled (B), Disabled (0)
Letter 8: Hyper Bark mutator enabled (H), Disabled (0)
Letter 9: Auto Bomb mutator enabled (A), Disabled (0)
Letter 10: Score Extends mutator enabled (S), Disabled (0)
Letter 11: Fruit Extends mutator enabled (F), Disabled (0)
Letter 12: Animal Spirit mutator enabled (A), Disabled (0)
Letter 13: Stop Time and Absorb mutator enabled (S), Absorb only mutator enabled (A), Disabled (0)
Letter 14: Bark achievement state: (-) waiting for bark, the user should bark at least one time to unlock the bark achievement. (B) Bark achievement active. Red cross over the letter means the achievements have been lost.
Letter 15: One Life achievement state: (L) achievement active. Red cross over the letter means the achievements have been lost.
Letter 16: Pacifist achievement state: (P) achievement active. Red cross over the letter means the achievements have been lost.
Letter 17: Finish the game in a specific difficulty achievement state: (-) difficulty too low for the achievement. (H) corgiest difficulty achievement active. (I) ultra nightmare difficulty achievement active. Red cross over the letter means the achievements have been lost.

[h2][b]Fixes and Balance:[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Change side is unlocked from the start and it's faster.
[*] Increased the invulnerability time and improved the visual effect. Shows a shield animation when the player has respawned or an auto bomb has been triggered.
[*] Improved the power up attraction algorithm

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/19e49f3a3dd997a456223d62a8dc1f7353266a61.jpg[/img]
Hello Everyone,

Mission Control here! first of all we want to thanks to all of you who has purchased and supported [b]ProtoCorgi[/b]. The game was released in [url=https://kemonogames.com/2023/06/23/protocorgi-is-finally-available-on-steam-epic-game-store-and-switch/]july 15th[/url] and since them the reception of the game has been mostly positive, and we’re really happy and proud for that.

So, [b]we are working on the [u]version 1.1[/u] of the game[/b]. This patch will be focused on improvements and solutions to the common issues we see looking at the livestreams and comments of the game. This is a sneak preview of what we’re working.

The first big change is the revamped Pause menu! We know that some people have been confused by the original ProtoCorgi pause screen. To remedy that we decided to made a new redesigned pause menu. We changed the color of the message tooltip to brown and the possibility of modifying some options without the need to leave a session.
[previewyoutube=T8YqNt8zi-U;full][/previewyoutube]
One of those new options is [b]brightness support[/b]. This change aims to make the game more accessible, as we heard some players had trouble distinguishing enemies, bullets and the background. We hope this can fix some visual problems on ProtoCorgi.

The new five options are:

[b]Background brightness[/b] = self explained
[b]Effects brightness[/b] = brightness on explosions, particles, full screen explosions, etc
[b]Snack brightness[/b] = brightness of the snacks that orbit around Bullet’s combo
[b]Ally bullet brightness[/b] = brightness of player shots
[b]Score brightness[/b] = brightness of the score texts that come out when you get points
[previewyoutube=7ggcn9f58Eg;full][/previewyoutube]
Probably the biggest change is in [b]the BARK shoot[/b]: the original bark is designed as a neutral, low power, safe shoot, just in case the weapon upgrade picked is not the best. The bark can be used to pick fruits and reveal hidden chests. The bark is also consumed in this action, as we placed the chests in a way that they should not block user shoots from approaching enemies. Still as we have multiple difficulties with level designs changes, this is not easy doable and there is still missing places where the user can get killed by the chests or fruits consuming bark bullets.

The most offending place we can think of is the one shown in this video in pup/puppest difficulties:
[previewyoutube=camoY4X11_0;full][/previewyoutube]
So we could balance the whole game by moving the chest in different difficulties to fix the problem or we could redesign the bark in a way that this doesn’t happen.

We choose the second option. We plan to implement the [b]HYPERBARK[/b] mechanic, when the Bark bullet hits a fruit or a chest, instead of consuming the bark, the bark gets powered up, increasing the size and the damage and this can be chained.
[previewyoutube=2xLGvkRSXDc;full][/previewyoutube]
We think this is the best solution for the problem that creates new strategies and open for better level design ideas with the chests.

There is also some small changes and [b]some surprises[/b] that we don’t want to reveal right now, but those are by far the most important. Of course we are open for feedback if you want to suggests some ideas, and please don’t forget that we have an [url=https://kemonogames.com/2023/06/28/protocorgi-faq/]official ProtoCorgi FAQ[/url] in our website that we’re updating from time to time. Hello Everyone,

Mission Control here! Today we want to talk to you about the dangers that lurk in the depth of space. At the end of each stage in [i]ProtoCorgi[/i], Bullet’s danger sensors will go off and you will meet a terrible fate: A boss encounter!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/754832b4ddc309c8be730126834b7469aa168a9d.png[/img]

Each boss comes with a unique set of attacks and movements. Those of you who have made it to the end of the demo will have already met one of them: [b]The Guardian Eye![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/6477105b456af0e2358684d8eb8cf121e3c8a146.png[/img]
(Hey Buddy, what are you looking at?!)

He shoots lasers out of his pupil and tries to crush Bullet like the oversized ping-pong ball he is. Don’t let him succeed! If you pay attention, you might be able to predict his path – make sure to take advantage of that! To defeat him, you will need good aim and the right timing. Of course, these are just his warmup attacks – just wait until you meet him in the full version, where he will have a few more tricks up his none-existing sleeves. 

All the bosses you will encounter in [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] have strengths and weaknesses like this. Some are more obvious than others. Of course, your chances of success also depend on which weapons you have equipped. notes.notes:
Hello Everyone, 

Mission Control here! Thank you all so much for watching our stream and playing the new [i]ProtoCrogi[/i] demo during Steam Next Fest – we’ve been overjoyed by the amount of positive feedback we received from you! 

Today we want to show off another feature of both the demo and the full version: difficulty settings!
One of our goals for [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] was to make it accessible to a broad range of people. The shoot’em up games of the 80s were thrillingly difficult – since this is almost a genre staple, it wasn’t something we wanted to lose. 

At the same time, it is that very characteristic that also made them very frustrating for a lot of people: those with little time on their hands to practice, those simply wishing to play for the joy of experiencing the levels, or even just those with little patience. We wanted to make sure that as many people as possible would be able to love Bullet, as well as enjoy shoot’em up games. 

The result of our musings: Difficulty settings!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/d78b2ae4f26cd1b2aee8c49931d68369f78d9f3a.jpg[/img]

There are many different challenges for you to unlock: from Pup to Puppest to the elusive Ultra Nightmare! The full version of [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] will include a whooping nine different difficulties! 
Now, you might wonder what these difficulties will actually look like in-game:

The first difference is the amount of enemies you will encounter. At Ultra Nightmare, Bullet will have his paws full shooting everything in sight! The second difference are the types of enemies you encounter at different stages of the game, as well as their level of aggression. Watch out for vicious attacks from behind! 

The same is true for the bosses: more health and a more aggressive attitude to beat! They might also use different strategies to strike you down: the higher the difficulty, the more it will keep you on your toes. Quick reactions are the name of the game!

Will you challenge yourself on Ultra Nightmare? Or go for a not-so-leisure stroll as a pup? 

At the end of the day, remember: Playing [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] on a lower difficulty doesn’t say anything about your skills. It simply means a different way of enjoying the game 😊 

[b]*Mission Control, over*[/b]

Hello Everyone, 

It’s Mission Control again! Today, we want to introduce you to the story of [i]ProtoCorgi[/i], particularly the back story of Bullet’s adventure. For those who would rather see it than read about it, have a look at our new Prologue trailer right here:

[previewyoutube=NVGPUbSCyr4;full][/previewyoutube]

Our story begins with Bullet’s rebirth at the hands of Nixie, an amazing military scientist, who is also Bullet’s owner and best friend. To bring the most important dog in her life back to the land of  the living, she moved heaven and earth and employed dangerous, previously untested military technology. 

The result was a dog-robot unlike any other: Equipped with destructive, multidirectional weapons, aggressive barking loud enough to rip enemies apart and the ability to survive infinitely in open space, it was more weapon than dog. The final puzzle piece of her creation: Bullet’s essence – to transfer the memories, spirit and golden soul that really made up the best friend she missed so much. 

Just as Nixie is about to complete her most ambitious masterpiece, disaster strikes! 
The evil army of space aliens Nixie’s military fraction has been defending the universe against attack her laboratory and kidnap her for their own nefarious purposes. Just before all would be lost, Nixie hits Bullet’s activation button! 
Now active, Bullet manages to escape certain death and meets up with Nick – an amazing military pilot. 

To strike back and save Nixie, Nick immediately enters his mecha and launches a counter attack against the enemy. However, their opponents came prepared – fearing Nick’s revenge, they brought an incredible secret weapon: a brain washing parasite. Unable to interfere, Bullet is forced to watch helplessly as Nick turns against him and his former comrades and joins the evil space army.


And this is finally were we meet Bullet. At the beginning of the most important journey of his life: Alone and devastated, but unbroken and more determined than ever to save the most important person in his life. 

Will Bullet’s power and determination be enough to defeat his enemies? Can he survive the many dangers he will face at the very edge of the universe? Can he save Nixie against all odds? …and what will become of Nick?

That is up to you! To find out if Bullet succeeds, play [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] when it comes out here on Steam on August 26th.

notes.title: Space Tunes for Space Dogs
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/eb435745fe233f5c6c29c68a9787f0a229f33a6d.jpg[/img]

Hello Everyone,

Mission Control here. This week we would like to introduce you to the fantastic soundtrack of [i]ProtoCorgi[/i]. After all, it is a truth universally acknowledged that a Corgi on a potentially deadly mission needs the right tunes to get amped up and get into the zone to obliterate his enemies!

To get the best result possible, all music for [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] was hand made by [i]Kemono Games[/i]’ very own composer Francisco Cerda, in cooperation with Bullet himself! But we are going to let the man speak for himself 😊 


[b]Q: First question: Who or what inspired you, Francisco?[/b]

[b]A: [/b]The first time we met to talk about [i]ProtoCorgi[/i]’s soundtrack, our CEO, Mario, shared a bunch of musical references. Most of them were the kind of Japanese electronic shoot’em up music featured in games such as DoDonPachi, Mushihimesama Futari, Tohou, etc.
I liked a lot of what I heard, but still wanted to give our music a special flavor in order to differentiate us. Since [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] has strong roots in 16 and 32 bit Japanese videogames, the sound of 80’s & 90’s Anime seemed like a natural fit. Thus, a mixture was born, which took the reoccurring electronic sound heard in several Bullet Hell games, along with the old school jazzy/funk/disco arrangements found in the golden era of Japan animation.
There’s also a big influence of other genres I discovered along the way, such as Future Core, Future Funk and City Pop.


[b]Q: What was your goal when you created the soundtrack for [i]ProtoCorgi[/i]? How did you want people to feel?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] I wanted to make memorable music, melodies that stuck from the first hearing, the same way as happened to me with videogames I played in my youth. The music is arranged in a way that reinforces the Kawaii themes presented in [i]ProtoCorgi[/i], conveying an epic but yet “uwu” feel at the same time.


[b]Q: What do you think is unique about the music?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] I think that the old school jazzy harmonic progressions are a big part of what makes this soundtrack different. It brings back an outdated way of making music, in a world where “four chord songs” are the rule.


[b]Q: Did you encounter any challenges?[/b]

[b]A: [/b]The hardest part is to keep up with the expectations. The music previews I’ve shared on Soundcloud already had an awesome reception, so the pressure is high every time I start with a new track. However, I’m pretty confident in the material we’ve crafted so far. Is not always in the same style as the trailer song everybody loves, but it has the same melodic-emotional energy.


[b]Q: Finally, is there any part you like particularly well?[/b]

[b]A: [/b]We’ve done a bunch of songs with Japanese lyrics for the game’s opening and ending, and also for some in-game sequences. I really enjoy those. They gave [b]ProtoCorgi[/b] an intense Anime feel, which is something I’ve always dreamt of making music for!


And now you have heard from the master himself how [i]ProtoCorgi[/i]’s soundtrack came about! 
You can listen to a sneak peak of the soundtrack [url=https://soundcloud.com/franciscofoco/protocorgi-level-1-theme]here[/url]

[b]!Warning![/b]: Do not play these tunes for your Corgi at home. We do not take responsibility for damages to your life or property!

Hello Everyone, 

Mission Control here. As promised, this week we want to give you an insight into [i]ProtoCorgi[/i]’s visual design. Without further ado, we present: Bullet’s Space Odyssey – Guaranteed to make you nostalgic for a place you’ve never been!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/54ac669466497484554db0183e61951abcfbdfde.png[/img]
(In space, no one hears you bark!)

Just like the game itself, the retro pixel art style of [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] was inspired by old Konami and particularly Treasure games from the SNES and arcade era. They were an important part of our childhood and still define the genre today, so we really wanted to invoke that same feeling. Choosing retro pixel art for [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] was an easy choice. 

That doesn’t mean we didn’t take advantage of how much more you can do with it today, however!
There is far more room for details and vibrant colours now then there was in the 80s, and we tried to take full advantage of that to make the game as lively and playful as possible. Bullet turned out particularly expressive: Try to spot all his different expressions when you play the Demo! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/d8d2f48b954017e369ce105a03269f4f0b560b21.png[/img]                     [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/aedbd06dd4b16479dc702323607754e6c3bf6a23.png[/img] 
([i]Bullet - So done with all these space aliens vs Bullet - Ready for action![/i]) 

Even though with [i]ProtoCorgi[/i], we are aiming at a modernized approach to the shoot’em up genre, we definitely didn’t want to lose the retro shmup identity. We really like how the end result looks, but we will leave the final judgement up to you! 


Maybe unsurprisingly, Anime was another major source of inspiration for us, which you can see particularly in the design of Bullet and Nixie here in this concept art. The goal was to invoke everything we love and remember so well from our own childhood and to share that appreciation with you.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/0ff67ef3ff8ad940021c064dc90a1ec6d842ec94.jpg[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34624825/1d21b028f0bd531d687dd72e8c3c9b29c357d56a.jpg[/img]

Nixie already looks a lot like her final design here – the big eyes and lack of nose are pretty common for anime. And look at little Bullet, what a ferocious bark! Such a big shot for such a small guy, that part hasn’t changed much since his conception. If you are now wondering about Bullet’s enemies – no worries, they will take centre stage in a later post.


And now we are at the end of Bullet’s Space Odyssey. Did it awaken your nostalgia? Are you inspired to fire up your old SNES and dig out that first shoot’em up game you ever played? Or maybe you just want to fire up the [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] demo and get lost in bright, dangerous outer space!

Whichever it is, we really hope you will like the look of [i]ProtoCorgi[/i] once the full game comes out.

notes.title: ProtoCorgi Demo Update 0.26!
notes.notes:
Hello Guys!

Here is a new update of the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1039280/ProtoCorgi/][b]ProtoCorgi Demo[/b][/url], and this is a big one! 

We fixed almost all of the bugs, better powerup management, giant fruits, some optimizations and reworked the menu with more options!
Feels like a new game now!

[b]Changelog of 0.26:[/b]

[list]
[*] When the player get a new powerup drop the old one at max level.
[*] Anemone body health is reduced in later difficulties making them harder to deal with homing missiles.
[*] Added giant fruits.
[*] Menu reworked with framerate, full screen, screen scale and many more options!.
[*] Pool most used scenes at start.
[*] Reworked bullet system, fixes bullet layering problems, bullets dying if the enemy dies or anemone plasma beams outside sceen/after eye dying.
[*] Fixed black hole attraction, detached anemone eyes work as intended now.
[*] Fixed analog not working in menu.
[*] Added secret codes.
[*] Enemies can't be damaged or damage player outside screen. No more turret snails dying outside screen doing nothing.
[*] Animations don't run if the objects are outside screen.
[/list]

notes.title: ProtoCorgi Update. Now avalaible for Mac and Linux!
notes.notes:
Hello Guys!

We updated the ProtoCorgi Demo! Avalaible now for Mac and Linux!:

We implemented many changes from initial version (0.16), the most relevant ones are a complete rework of systems and difficulty, change side holding a button, lock option rotation, progression, shorten tutorials, full screen support and more! 

Detailed Changelog:

[b]v0.25.7:[/b]
[list]
[*] ❤❤❤ Hitbox is represented now by a heart ❤❤❤
[*] Fixed Mac and Linux Steam depots.
[*] Options rotation lock added when the player is shooting.
[*] Shield Bomb damages enemies and makes the player invulnerable.
[*] Overdrive Bomb orbs damage enemies.
[*] Better difficulty curve, more easy at early levels, same difficulty at end levels.
[*] Shorten tutorials.
[*] Fish ship master can't shot behind.
[*] Turret snail shot are limited in early difficulties.
[*] Greatly reduced Guardian Eye Boss health points in early difficulties.
[/list]
[b]v0.25.5:[/b]
[list]
[*] Added full screen support (alt + enter).
[*] Added more music.
[/list]
[b]v0.25:[/b]
[list]
[*] Reworked suicide bullet system.
[*] Reworked the speed of bullets and enemies in all difficulties.
[*] Added alt, shift and control key support.
[/list]
[b]v0.24:[/b]
[list]
[*] QoL galore.
[*] Reworked the powerup system.
[*] Player could change side holding Animal Spirit button.
[*] Magnet behavior for fruits and  player death drops.
[*] Added progression.
[/list]
[b]v0.20:[/b]
[list]
[*] QoL changes.
[*] Highscores per difficulty.
[/list]
[b]v0.16:[/b]
[list]
[*] Demo uploaded.
[/list]
